_doc: FROZEN legacy ledger of versioned migration artifacts for the first-party
core store schema (buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries / createStoreTables in
src/lib/drizzle-store.ts). This array is shipped history: the CI gate
rejects ANY change to its entries and ANY new entry appended to it.
NEW migrations author a per-migration fragment at
migrations/manifest.d/core__NNNN_short-description.json instead (same
filename stem as the runner module; one file per migration, so
concurrent migration PRs never conflict on a shared tail — cinatra#1335).
Every consumer reads the ledger as the deterministic UNION of this array
and the fragments, via migrations/manifest-reader.mjs. Entry shape (both
forms):
seq         — the NNNN sequence number, as a string ('0001')
file        — the artifact path relative to migrations/ (runner-module
entries: 'core/core__NNNN_short-description.mjs'; seq
0001/0002 predate the node-pg-migrate runner and point at
the legacy psql artifacts — their runner forms live at
core/core__0001_… and core/core__0002_…; those two
entries stay in this frozen array permanently)
summary     — one line: what the migration does and why
destructive — true when the change affects user-land data (the case
that REQUIRES an artifact); false for optional artifacts
shipped with additive changes (e.g. long backfills)
tables      — the affected core-store table names (no schema prefix;
the schema name is variable, see the README)
Never renumber or rewrite an entry once its migration has shipped;
supersede it with a new sequence number. 0021 and 0023 are permanent
gaps — the runner tolerates sequence gaps. (The hand-maintained SEQ
COORDINATION note that used to live here is retired: seq claims are now
per-file fragments, and the gate reds duplicate claims deterministically.)

migrations.summary: Add notifications.dedupe_key + partial unique index (user_id, dedupe_key) for the general per-user notification dedupe (issue #50). Required by the unique-index-on-existing-table rule; cannot collide in practice — the column is new, so every pre-existing row is outside the partial-index predicate.

Drop the dead agent_templates.durable column (issue #84). No routing/execution code ever read it and every writer only persisted the default false, so no user-land data is lost; required by the drop-column-on-existing-table rule.

Drop the dormant extension_migrations ledger (issue #118): it backed the RETIRED extension JSON-DSL migration machinery and was empty on every lineage (no extension ever declared cinatra.migrations). Extension migrations now record into the shared node-pg-migrate pgmigrations ledger under ext_<scope>_<pkg>__NNNN names; required by the drop-table rule.

Demote the 17 anchor rows the requiredExtensions shrink (cinatra#7) removed from the prod bootable set (33 -> 16): required_in_prod -> false and locked -> active for exactly those rows; archived tombstones stay archived; nothing is uninstalled and all provenance/dependency/owner state is preserved. Fresh databases seed from the current declaration and ledger-fake the chain; idempotent on re-run.

Convert the extension install-op journal to APPEND-ONLY (cinatra#158): drop the two single-row-per-(package,org) unique indexes (pkg_org_uniq / pkg_global_uniq), add partial-UNIQUE indexes enforcing at most one finalized op per (package,org) (the install anchor) + the global org_id-IS-NULL twin, add a (package_name, org_id, phase) scan index, and widen the phase CHECK to admit the new terminal 'superseded' phase. Existing rows are preserved (append-only is strictly more permissive than single-row, so the new partial-unique-on-finalized cannot collide: a single-row schema had at most one row per (package,org), hence at most one finalized). COORDINATED, NON-ROLLING boundary: apply with pre-0005 writers drained — old reset-on-begin UPDATE keyed by (package,org) could touch multiple appended rows once the full unique indexes are gone.

One-time, lossy-by-design canonicalization of legacy dashboard configs to the v1.2 analytics envelope (cinatra#327; owner decision eng#206 — NO backward compat, the strict validator stays strict and #329 deletes the legacy parser). Rewrites every dashboards row AND dashboard_revisions row at config_version IN ('1.0.0','1.1.0') into the SAME single-analytics-portlet v1.2 envelope #326's wrapDcAsV12 emits ({apiVersion:'v1.2', scopeLevel:<derived>, portlets:[{instanceId/kind:'analytics', version:'1.0.0', slot:'fixed', config:{dashboard:<normalized 1.1-shaped config>, __cinatraMigration:'core__0006'}}]}) and sets config_version='v1.2'. A JS-side TOTAL normalizer (bundled into the module; pinned EQUIVALENT to the package validators by a unit test) runs INSIDE the migration transaction via parameterized UPDATE ... SET config_json=$1::jsonb: it NEVER throws and ALWAYS yields a config.dashboard passing the analytics kind's strict DashboardConfigV1_1Schema deep validator, repairing not just well-formed 1.0/1.1 bodies but corrupt-at-rest shapes (scalar/null/array root -> minimal-valid-empty dashboard; dashboardFilterMapping:'bad'->[]; eagerLoad:'yes'->dropped; grid:{cols:-1}->dropped; layoutMode:'freeform'->'grid'; colorPalette:42->dropped; non-object portlet element dropped; missing/empty id -> deterministic unique id; missing content-spec -> analysisConfig:{}); conforming known data is preserved byte-equivalent (passthrough keys kept). Each wrapped envelope is FINAL-VALIDATED by the bundled validator before write; any failure ABORTS the transaction. A migration MARKER is stamped at portlets[0].config.__cinatraMigration (a strict-allowed opaque-record slot) so down() reverts ONLY rows THIS migration produced. scopeLevel derives from the row's project_id/template_scope (-> 'project') else owner_level; revisions JOIN dashboards on dashboard_id for scope (revisions carry no scope columns). Both tables are LOCKed IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE before the selects (the runner's advisory lock serializes schema work, not app dashboard writes) and a zero-legacy COUNT(*) postcondition asserts no 1.0/1.1 row remains. Also flips the EXISTING-DB dashboards.config_version column DEFAULT '1.0.0' -> 'v1.2' (distinct from the fresh-install bootstrap-DDL/Drizzle-mirror default, also flipped this PR). Idempotent (the legacy-version predicate excludes already-v1.2 rows; the normalizer is a fixed point on conforming bodies). down() reverses ONLY marker-bearing single-analytics-portlet rows (exactly one portlet AND portlets[0].kind='analytics' AND portlets[0].config.__cinatraMigration='core__0006' AND extension_id IS NULL), unwrapping back to the bare DC config + config_version '1.1.0' and resetting the column default, so genuine extension v1.2 rows, NON-migrated multi-portlet operator v1.2 rows (analytics-first + siblings), AND native #326 single-analytics operator v1.2 rows (no marker) are all untouched.

Add the agent_run_pm_links link table for the schedule↔PM-task sync (cinatra#317): one row per schedule-defining trigger mirrored to an external project-management provider (Plane), keyed by run_id (one-to-one with agent_run_triggers) with FK run_id → agent_runs.id ON DELETE CASCADE, plus a (provider) scan index. Columns: provider (PM provider id), external_task_id (provider work-item id; null until first successful push), synced_at (last successful mirror), sync_error (last fail-open error; null=healthy), version (optimistic-concurrency counter for the reconcile loop #318). ADDITIVE (a brand-new table) so no artifact is strictly required — it rides the idempotent bootstrap DDL (buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries adds the same CREATE TABLE/INDEX this PR); the module ships anyway as a pure CREATE … IF NOT EXISTS to keep the fresh-bootstrap and migration paths aligned and give the table a ledgered row (no-op on a bootstrap-seeded schema, ledger-faked on a fresh install). down() drops the index then the table.

Add the webhook_idempotency leased dedupe ledger for the generic inbound-webhook route (cinatra#340): one row per (scope, site_id, message_id) where scope is '<vendor>/<slug>/<hook>' and message_id is the Standard-Webhooks webhook-id. Leased state machine (processing | done | failed) with lease_until + attempt_count (the finalize fence) so a crashed holder's lease expires and a later arrival re-claims, and a stale holder cannot overwrite a newer attempt's verdict. All three key columns NOT NULL with a UNIQUE index (scope, site_id, message_id); site_id uuid (connect_sites.site_id identity space, D1b). ADDITIVE (a brand-new table) — rides the idempotent bootstrap DDL (buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries adds the same CREATE TABLE/INDEX this PR); the module ships anyway as a pure CREATE … IF NOT EXISTS (no-op on a bootstrap-seeded schema, ledger-faked on a fresh install). down() drops the index then the table.

Add the webhook_secret_bindings table for the per-webhook/per-site secret service (cinatra#340): one active row per (vendor, slug, hook, site) holding the Standard-Webhooks secret material ENCRYPTED via the host secretsCodec (current_secret_ciphertext/iv + an optional previous_secret_ciphertext/iv for the bounded dual-secret rotation window, previous_expires_at, rotated_at), resolved by the server-issued opaque binding_id (PRIMARY KEY) — never from the request payload. site_id uuid (connect_sites.site_id space, D1b). A partial UNIQUE index (vendor, slug, hook, site_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL enforces at most one active binding per tuple; revoked_at tombstones a binding. legacy_enabled is the structural hook for the #343 legacy single-shared-secret bridge (its legacy-secret STORAGE columns are deferred to #343 per D3c option A; stays false in #340). ADDITIVE (a brand-new table) — rides the idempotent bootstrap DDL; ships as a pure CREATE … IF NOT EXISTS (no-op on a bootstrap-seeded schema, ledger-faked on a fresh install). down() drops the indexes then the table.

Add the webhook_outbound_dead_letter table for the host-owned OUTBOUND webhook delivery engine (cinatra#341): the durable dead-letter record the pre-#341 fire-and-forget assistant-webhook path lacked. The WEBHOOK_OUTBOUND_DELIVERY BullMQ dispatcher arm writes one row when a delivery is classified `permanent` (non-retryable 4xx, missing url/secret, or a non-decodable legacy secret the standardwebhooks signer rejects) OR when all configured `attempts` are exhausted on a `retryable` result. Columns: event_kind (e.g. 'assistant.mention'), message_id (the Standard-Webhooks webhook-id / receiver idempotency key), target_url (reduced to origin+pathname — query string + userinfo stripped so a URL token can't leak), payload_digest (sha256 hex of the serialized payload — NEVER the raw payload or secret), attempts, last_status (int|null), last_error (truncated+scrubbed text), failed_at, created_at. A UNIQUE index (event_kind, message_id) makes the DLQ insert idempotent (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING — a permanent row and a later last-attempt-retryable row for the same identity collapse to one) and a failed_at scan index backs the operator view. ADDITIVE (a brand-new table) — rides the idempotent bootstrap DDL (buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries adds the same CREATE TABLE/INDEX this PR); the module ships anyway as a pure CREATE … IF NOT EXISTS (no-op on a bootstrap-seeded schema, ledger-faked on a fresh install). down() drops the indexes then the table.

Add the legacy single-shared-secret STORAGE columns (legacy_secret_ciphertext/iv) to webhook_secret_bindings for the #343 legacy webhook bridge (D3c option A) deferred by core__0009. A binding flagged legacy_enabled keeps its in-field sender's bespoke `sha256=<hex>` HMAC (the deployed WordPress plugin) while still routing through the generic /webhook facility; the shared HMAC secret is stored ENCRYPTED via the host secretsCodec (ciphertext+iv blob, NOT a ref) under a field-scoped AAD (webhook-binding.<binding_id>.legacy) so a legacy blob can never decrypt in the current/previous columns. Both columns nullable — a Standard-Webhooks binding (the forward default) leaves them null. ADDITIVE + idempotent (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS) — rides the idempotent bootstrap DDL (buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries adds the same columns); no-op on a bootstrap-seeded schema, ledger-faked on a fresh install. down() drops the two columns.

One-time rewrite of legacy GTM-era persisted tokens to their Cinatra names, retiring the runtime normalization in the hot core-store path (cinatra-ai/engineering#309). The removed src/lib/database.ts normalizePersistedString/normalizePersistedValue pass rewrote pre-rebrand persisted values on EVERY core-store parse and write (@gtm-central/… scopes, GTM Central/GTM Center display names, gtm_central_… snake_case keys, the …/openai-local-shell:latest skill-shell image ref, the gtmcentral.app/gtm.center hosts); that read-time self-healing is now removed, so this migration rewrites the remaining at-rest tokens ONCE. up() discovers — inside the migration transaction, from information_schema in current_schema() — the metadata.value JSON column plus every other table with a textual payload column (the (id, payload) JSON-row stores the normalization wrote through: startups, startup_overrides, skill_packages, skills, notifications, campaigns, chat_threads, and any sibling store) and applies the EXACT in-order replace() chain the runtime normalization used (the order is load-bearing; a companion unit test pins the SQL token map against a JS reimplementation of the original chain and proves byte-equivalence + idempotency). Each UPDATE is gated on the column actually CONTAINING a GTM token (position(token in col) > 0 OR … — an EXACT substring test, not LIKE, because several tokens carry the LIKE wildcard _), so it is minimal-touch and idempotent (a re-run is a no-op once the tokens are gone) and JSON validity is preserved (substring rewrite of self-contained tokens). DATA REWRITE of existing user-land JSON, so an artifact is shipped (this module); the change is NOT a drizzle-store.ts schema change (no DDL), so it rides no bootstrap DDL — on a fresh install it ledger-fakes (no rows to rewrite) and on an existing deployment db migrate executes it. down() is a NO-OP: the rewrite is a lossy canonicalization of a retired vocabulary (e.g. all three …/openai-local-shell:latest variants collapse to cinatra/skill-shell:latest) and must not be re-introduced.

One-time backfill of agent_templates.org_id for install-seeded rows persisted with org_id = NULL and never claimed an org (cinatra-ai/cinatra#847). org_id is nullable by design ('NULL on freshly-installed templates … before backfill'); ensureAgentPackage → importAgentTemplateCore and the marketplace install saga wrote NULL and nothing backfilled it — not even after first run — so every org-scoped reader (readAgentTemplates' eq(org_id, :orgId); the /agents 'Installed agents' card's count(*) WHERE org_id = :orgId) excludes those rows and the dashboard shows 'Installed agents (0) — No agents installed yet' while the run portlets chart real runs. up() infers each NULL-org template's org from its agent_runs (org_id is NOT NULL and every run resolves the acting org): a template run under EXACTLY ONE org (HAVING count(DISTINCT org_id) = 1) is backfilled to that org; templates whose runs span MULTIPLE orgs are a tenant-isolation red flag and are DELIBERATELY left NULL (they need per-org cloning, not a single backfill); run-less templates are left NULL and claimed on first run by the going-forward set_agent_template_first_run trigger (extended in the same PR to COALESCE org_id from the run's org). Gated on t.org_id IS NULL so it is minimal-touch + idempotent (a re-run is a no-op); writes ONLY org_id (never owner_level/owner_id) so agent_owner_move_trg does not fire; never widens visibility across tenants (a template becomes visible only to the org that already owns its runs). DATA REWRITE of existing user-land rows, so an artifact is shipped (this module); the same PR extends the first_run trigger in the bootstrap DDL (buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries) so a fresh install is born at the post-migration shape and this chain ledger-fakes there (no rows to backfill), while db migrate executes it on an existing deployment. down() is a NO-OP: a backfilled org_id is indistinguishable from a natively-set one, so reverting it would corrupt legitimately owned rows and reintroduce the bug.

One-shot backfill of the new nango_connection identity table from the legacy SavedNangoConnection blobs (cinatra-ai/cinatra#951, W1 of the connector access-scoping epic #950). The nango gateway persists all saved connections as one JSON blob at metadata key connector_config:nango_connections ({connections:{[connectorKey]: SavedNangoConnection[]}}); the epic makes a connection an owner-bound entity, so up() creates EXACTLY ONE identity row per blob connection (ON CONFLICT on the live (connector_key, connection_id) partial-unique index skips already-present identities; the table itself is created by the bootstrap DDL in src/lib/drizzle-store.ts, same PR). Owner resolution is fail-closed and owner-confirmed (epic decision 3): (1) the recorded connecting user (entry.userId, verified against public."user") - covers scope:"user" and legacy scope:"app" entries that recorded the actor; (2) the installing org-admin via the connector package's canonical extension_access_policy.installed_by_user_id; (3) the earliest owner/admin member (public.member) of the resolved organization; otherwise the migration ABORTS - owner_user_id is NOT NULL by contract and a placeholder is never written. organization_id = the single distinct non-NULL org across the package's live installed_extension rows, else the deployment's sole organization, else NULL (nullable by design). connectorKey->package uses an explicit frozen map (unknown keys abort fail-closed). The whole backfill runs in ONE owned transaction (pgm.noTransaction + explicit BEGIN/COMMIT, LOCK nango_connection IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE - the core__0006 model) and writes a review report (per-row rule used, inserted ids, counts) to metadata key nango_connection_backfill_report:v1 IN THE SAME TRANSACTION (acceptance: backfill provenance recorded for review). down() deletes exactly the rows named in the report + the report key - live-connect-flow identity rows are untouched; no report = no-op (fresh/ledger-faked schemas).

One-shot per-connection GRANT seed + external-MCP identity seed (cinatra-ai/cinatra#952, W2 of the connector access-scoping epic #950). W1's core__0014 created nango_connection identity rows but NO extension_access_policy rows; W2's use-gate is fail-closed (explicit OWNER_DEFAULT fallback - no policy row = owner-only), so without this seed every legacy scope:"app" connection (org-shared by construction pre-epic) would silently stop working for everyone but its backfilled owner. Phase A (behavior-PRESERVING, not broadening - epic decision 3's legacy handling): every live identity row whose legacy blob entry is scope:"app" AND whose organization_id is NON-NULL gets one workspace-visibility policy row, ONLY when no policy row exists (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING - never resets a widened/narrowed policy); scope:"user" rows and ALL organization_id IS NULL rows get NOTHING (owner-only; a null-org row must never gain a workspace grant - workspace has no cross-org guard to contain it; codex W2 convergence, null-org narrowing). Phase B: external_mcp_servers rows carrying a nango_connection_id get identity rows (connector_key 'externalMcp', the host sentinel package id - external-MCP connections have NO blob record and are NOT in the 0014 key->package map), owner resolved fail-closed mirroring 0014 ((1) row user_id verified against public."user", (2) earliest owner/admin of the row's org, (3) earliest owner/admin of the deployment's sole organization, else ABORT); non-user-scope rows with a non-NULL resolved org additionally get the workspace policy seed (instance-global by construction - the org-bound InternalWorker mint needs it). Same owned-transaction model as core__0014 (pgm.noTransaction + explicit BEGIN/COMMIT, SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE locks) and the same provenance contract: a review report at metadata key connection_grant_seed_report:v1 IN the transaction; down() deletes exactly the report-named policy rows + identity rows + the report key (no report = no-op on fresh/ledger-faked schemas). Fresh installs are born post-W2 (the save-seam seeds new connections at save time), so this chain ledger-fakes there.

Reconcile the persisted accent palette to the pinned design spec's categorical set (cinatra-ai/cinatra#988 item 7, the high-risk half of the SIV listing-card conformance; companion UI PR carries items 1-6+8). EXTENSION_ACCENTS moves from the pre-reconciliation six (red/burgundy/indigo/green/mustard/slate) to the spec's seven categoricals (red/burgundy/green/rust/olive/plum/clay, docs@b35fdf4 design-system.html :root L31-37): indigo (the primary ACTION colour) and slate (the muted text colour) were never sanctioned banner grounds, mustard is not in the categorical set. Two persisted surfaces are reconciled independently, each in a fully guarded DO block (some lineages never provisioned these structures - a missing table/column is a clean no-op): public."user".accent_color (Avatar accent, user_accent_color_check) and <app schema>.extension_accent_color.accent_color (ExtensionCard accent). Order per surface: (1) drop every existing CHECK over the column FIRST, with names looked up from pg_constraint (never assumed) - the remapped values are outside the old union, (2) remap retired persisted values hue-nearest (indigo->plum, slate->plum, mustard->rust), (3) add the spec-set CHECK (NULL stays allowed - unset means derive). down() restores the six-colour CHECK after remapping the four new values back into the old union (rust->mustard, olive->green, plum->indigo, clay->red); the remap is documented LOSSY both ways - a palette retirement, not a rename. Idempotent: every step re-checks the live catalog, so re-runs and never-provisioned schemas are no-ops. Fresh installs ledger-fake the chain; the bootstrap DDL carries no accent structures, so there is no fresh-shape CREATE text to update.

Org-anchor backfill + identity-collision merge + connector org-anchor normalization (cinatra-ai/cinatra#1125, P0 of the admin-extension-parity epic #1124; backward compatibility is NOT a concern). Eliminates the org-less asymmetry class that no org admin could reach: (A) CONNECTOR org-anchor invariant — every connector installed_extension row that is not already a valid org anchor (owner_level='organization' AND owner_id = organization_id) and not a platform/workspace bundle anchor is normalized to owner_level='organization', owner_id = organization_id (covers user/team-owned connectors and malformed organization-tier rows), matching the canonical connector resolver's org-only query; (B) generic USER-owned backfill — org-less non-connector rows (owner_level='user' AND organization_id IS NULL) get organization_id set to the owning user's organization; (C) nango org backfill — live org-less nango_connection identity rows get organization_id set the same way (the residue core__0014 could not resolve at creation). Org resolution is fail-safe (a user's SOLE public.member organization, a team's public.team.organizationId, each verified against public."organization"; 0/>1 memberships => LEFT org-less, never guessed). Collision merge is deterministic (the existing org row WINS): backfilling to a taken identity tuple (organization_id, owner_level, owner_id, package_name) merges the loser into the survivor — extension_access_policy adopted onto the survivor only when it has none (else the loser's is dropped, survivor wins, full dropped policy recorded for audit), extension_co_owners UNIONed, the loser manifest row deleted; all dependent-row ops scoped by (resource_kind = loser.kind, resource_id = loser.id). Same owned-transaction model as core__0014 (pgm.noTransaction + explicit BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK; LOCK installed_extension, extension_access_policy, extension_co_owners, nango_connection IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE) with a provenance report at metadata key 'org_anchor_backfill_report:v1' written in the same transaction. Idempotent: a re-run mutates no target table (resolved rows fall out of their predicate, merged losers are gone, unresolvable rows are deterministically re-skipped and remain platform-admin-only, expected ~zero). A companion guard in packages/extensions/src/lifecycle-primitive.ts rejects non-org connector anchors going forward. down() is a NO-OP: a backfilled organization_id is indistinguishable from a native one and the merge deletes loser rows, so a revert would corrupt anchored rows; the ledger row records the run and the report preserves exactly what changed. Fresh installs are born at the post-migration shape and ledger-fake the chain.

One-time backfill of agent_runs.obo_ceiling (the agent on-behalf-of scope-ceiling chain, cinatra-ai/cinatra#1050) for runs that predate the column. The column is added nullable by the bootstrap DDL (buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries, same PR) and written going-forward at run creation; the MCP-token mint path re-derives the chain from the run's LOCKED template anchor and FAILS CLOSED when the persisted chain is absent or non-containing, so a pre-existing NULL run would degrade to the machine-token fallback at mint. up() backfills those rows deterministically from the run's org + project launch + its template's locked owner anchor, mirroring the shared deriveOboCeilingChain helper EXACTLY: a known non-org owner tier (user/team/workspace/project) with an empty/absent id is a corrupt anchor left NULL (fails closed at mint, never widened to org); owner_level='organization' -> {organization, owner_id||org_id}; null/missing-template/unrecognized owner tier -> no owner element; EVERY non-null chain carries a mandatory {organization, run.org_id} floor (deduped); an explicit project launch appends an independent {project, project_id} element (deduped). The same agreement with the helper is asserted on a real Postgres by the wave's live proof. Gated on obo_ceiling IS NULL so it is minimal-touch + idempotent; a fresh install is born at the post-column shape and holds no runs, so this chain ledger-fakes there while db migrate executes it against an existing deployment. down() is a NO-OP: a backfilled chain is indistinguishable from a going-forward write, so reverting would strip legitimate chains and reintroduce the fail-closed-at-mint degradation. Additive nullable column plus an optional backfill artifact (not a user-land data rewrite of an existing column), so destructive=false.

The interaction axis on agent_templates (cinatra-ai/cinatra#1037 P1, schema half). Adds agent_kind ('assistant'|'executor', default 'executor') and the typed assistant_config sidecar (JSON-as-text), plus two authoritative write-time invariants — agent_templates_agent_kind_check (agent_kind IN ('assistant','executor')) and agent_templates_agent_kind_config_check (an 'assistant' row MUST carry a config; an 'executor' row MUST NOT). agent_kind is ORTHOGONAL to type (leaf|proxy|orchestrator) — not overloaded, no 'project' kind. The two columns are additive (bootstrap DDL adds them via ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS; a fresh install is born at the target shape and ledger-fakes this chain); the CHECK constraints over an already-populated table are the transformational half this module carries on the operator upgrade path. Every existing row defaults to executor/NULL and satisfies the pairing CHECK, so the constraint validates with no backfill (no pre-existing assistant rows — the column is brand new). Idempotent/lineage-tolerant: columns IF NOT EXISTS, constraints added only when absent (pg_constraint lookup against current_schema()), index IF NOT EXISTS. down() drops the constraints, the kind index, then the columns (structural addition, not a rename). destructive=true because it adds CHECK constraints over a table that already holds rows on main.

Run-token spine persistence (cinatra-ai/cinatra#1193, W1 of the run-identity-spine epic #1192): add agent_runs.run_token_hash (text, nullable) holding ONLY the sha256-hex of the random per-run credential minted at dispatch, plus a PARTIAL UNIQUE INDEX agent_runs_run_token_hash_uniq (run_token_hash) WHERE run_token_hash IS NOT NULL so a single server verifier resolves the run from a presented token with no newest-wins tie-break. The raw token is never stored — it rides only the WayFlow initial message (and, in a later wave, first-party callbacks). Adding a UNIQUE index to an existing table is destructive per migrations/README.md (artifact required), but cannot collide here: the column is brand-new so every pre-existing row is NULL and the partial predicate excludes all of them (the index is built over zero rows) — mirroring the notifications.dedupe_key precedent (core__0001). ADDITIVE + idempotent (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS + CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS), rides the bootstrap DDL (buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries adds the same column + index this PR) — no-op on a bootstrap-seeded schema, ledger-faked on a fresh install, executed by db migrate on an existing deployment. No noTransaction (the partial index over an all-NULL column is instant, not CONCURRENTLY). The resume/clone no-copy invariant is enforced in code (every agent_runs insert uses an explicit column whitelist; the hash is written only by the dispatcher's setAgentRunTokenHash before the blocking sendTask). down() drops the index then the column, restoring the pre-0020 shape (no data loss — the raw token was never persisted).

Version identity for installed extensions (cinatra-ai/cinatra#1040 S1, storage half). installed_extension gains version text NOT NULL (backfilled COALESCE(source->>'version','0.0.0') — verdaccio/bundled sources carry source.version, github/local carry none so the '0.0.0' floor is load-bearing) and is_default boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true; the two identity partial-unique indexes gain version (recreated under _v names, old names dropped) and a new one-default-per-identity partial-unique index pair enforces at most one default version per (org, owner, package) — safe on existing data because the pre-#1040 identity indexes were already unique on (org, owner, package) without version, so every existing row is the sole row for its identity. extension_install_ops gains version text NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.0.0' (no source column to derive from; a nullable version would let NULL-distinct admit two finalized rows per scope) and its finalized-anchor uniqueness is re-keyed to include version (precedent core__0005). Additive columns ride the idempotent bootstrap DDL (versionIdentitySchemaQueries spread into buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries, same PR) so a fresh install is born at the target shape and ledger-fakes this chain; the NOT NULL identity column + new unique indexes over already-populated tables are the transformational half this module carries on the operator upgrade path. Coordinated NON-rolling deploy boundary (core__0005): pre-0022 installed_extension inserts fail closed on the NOT NULL version, pre-0022 install-op finalizes write '0.0.0' and still supersede the prior anchor. Dynamic-dispatch primitive storage (cinatra-ai/cinatra#1032 deliverable 2): two brand-new tables. project_dispatch_attempts is the dispatch-attempt ledger — one row per deliberate dispatch attempt keyed UNIQUE (org_id, item_natural_key, action_version), written AHEAD of createAgentRun and carrying the deterministically derived idempotency_key passed VERBATIM to createAgentRun, so a tick crashing between dispatch and record cannot double-dispatch (the next tick re-begins the same key and agent_runs_idempotency_key_uniq resolves to the same child run); run_id is provenance with deliberately NO FK (append-only history outlives the run row); version is the optimistic-CAS counter (core__0007 shape). project_leases is the project-level lease keyed (org_id, project_ref) with heartbeat/expiry columns and a fencing version bumped on every (re)acquisition; stale-lease recovery = a conditional-upsert acquire that only wins when expires_at <= now() or the caller is the live holder. Both tables ride the idempotent bootstrap DDL (projectDispatchSchemaQueries spread into buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries, same PR); this module ships per the core__0007 precedent to keep fresh-bootstrap and operator-upgrade paths aligned — pure CREATE IF NOT EXISTS, no-op on a bootstrap-seeded schema, ledger-faked on a fresh install. down() drops both tables (fresh additions; exact pre-0024 shape on any lineage). destructive=false: brand-new tables, no user-land data affected.

Dependency edges move off the row jsonb (cinatra-ai/cinatra#1040 S2, edge-storage half). Creates extension_dependency_edge: one row per DECLARED manifest edge of an installed_extension row — declared_package_name / declared_kind / edge_type / requirement / version_constraint (the VersionConstraint union as jsonb, lossless round-trip) / declared_index (manifest array position; UNIQUE per dependent — positional, not a semantic dedupe) — plus the write-time RESOLUTION: resolved_install_id (WHICH installed row satisfied the edge; FK ON DELETE SET NULL) and resolution_reason (free-form provenance). The closure gates (boot/archive/restore/forward) validate resolved edges and fall back to the scoped name-lookup for unresolved ones. PREFLIGHT fails loudly on malformed legacy edges (naming dependent id + declared index) before any destructive work; the backfill resolves per-DECLARING-row scope (own-org live row first, then platform — a platform dependent binds only platform rows; default version preferred, deterministic id tie-break; missing target backfills unresolved) with DETERMINISTIC ids ('iede_' || md5(dependent:index)); then installed_extension.dependencies is DROPPED. The table rides the idempotent bootstrap DDL (dependencyEdgeSchemaQueries spread into buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries, same PR; the bootstrap CREATE of installed_extension no longer declares the jsonb column) so a fresh install is born at the target shape and ledger-fakes this chain; the backfill + column DROP over an already-populated table are the transformational half this module carries on the operator upgrade path. Structured assistant threads + assistant_turns (cinatra-ai/cinatra#1037 P2a, the assistant-runtime persistence half). SEQ COORDINATION: this slice originally reserved 0021 behind the sibling's 0020, then held 0023 (the claim ledger's hold after #1040 S1 shipped 0022) — but core__0024 (#1329) and core__0025 (#1331) shipped on main while this PR awaited final approval, and the shipped ledger is append-only with strictly-increasing tail seqs, so the pair lands at 0026, the next free sequence after the shipped head; 0021 and 0023 stay permanent gaps (rename-only renumber, no SQL change). Adds two typed tables: assistant_threads (the structured thread — owner_user_id, org_id, the bound assistant PRINCIPAL assistant_user_id, the A2A context_id continuity handle, title, ordering timestamps) and assistant_turns (one AG-UI RUN in a thread — thread_id FK, run_id keying the durable Redis-Streams AG-UI event log cinatra:a2a:events:{run_id}, assistant_user_id principal attribution, role, status). These own the #1037-P2 side of the assistant-stream boundary named in @cinatra-ai/agent-ui-protocol CONTRACT.md section 1 (thread model, message persistence, attribution, turn<->run linkage); the stream contract owns the durable event log itself, so assistant_turns stores metadata + the run pointer and NOT the events (no double persistence model). The legacy chat_threads JSON-payload table STAYS in place — the /chat persistence subroutes + chat_thread_send are rewired/deleted in P2b/P3 — so this migration is purely additive and introduces no double-write.
